nodes.name: Queue Sync Webhook
nodes.notes: Internal, same as 19/21. Nothing calls this automatically yet -- wiring it into 10 (lead capture) or 12 (book appointment) so syncs queue themselves on creation would mean editing already-live production workflows, deliberately out of scope here (same tradeoff as follow-up run advancement in 20). For now: call this manually/from elsewhere whenever something needs syncing.

parameters.query:
select
  (select id from tenants where slug = $1) as tenant_id,
  case $2
    when 'contact' then (select id from contacts where id = $3::uuid and tenant_id = (select id from tenants where slug = $1))
    when 'lead' then (select id from leads where id = $3::uuid and tenant_id = (select id from tenants where slug = $1))
    when 'appointment' then (select id from appointments where id = $3::uuid and tenant_id = (select id from tenants where slug = $1))
  end as entity_id;

nodes.name: Verify Entity Belongs To Tenant
nodes.notes: Scalar subqueries again, same reason as 21's resolver -- always exactly one row, entity_id comes back NULL rather than the item vanishing if the tenant/entity combo doesn't actually match. This is a real safety check, not just validation: without it, one tenant could queue a sync for another tenant's data by guessing a UUID.

nodes.name: Insert Sync Log
nodes.notes: No dedup -- calling this twice for the same entity creates two log rows. Acceptable for an audit-log-shaped table (crm_sync_log has no unique constraint to conflict on); the sweep just processes both. Not worth adding dedup logic without a real usage pattern showing it's actually a problem.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ success: false, error: 'tenant not found, or entity_id does not belong to this tenant' }) }}
